answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove collusion or fabricated work. A glacier-slow withdrawal delay gives disputes time to surface, while the stake limits how many identities an attacker can fund at once. Calling an old credential a relic or a new account a nebula changes nothing: each still needs capital, and a successful attack risks losing it.
